target_domain: JUCE VST Audio Plugin Development with Sound Design Integration

source_integration.description: This playbook integrates ALL content from previous versions, reference files, and firecrawl-harvested data.

contributed: EM-xx failure modes from Epiphany Machine v3
FM-01 to FM-23 generic JUCE failure modes

roles.human: Creative director, sound designer, final decision-maker on ALL audio/UX choices. Defines WHAT the plugin does and HOW it should sound. Every creative decision is human_only — AI asks, never assumes.
roles.ai: Code architect, implementation engine, reviewer, test generator. Handles HOW to build what's defined. Never makes creative decisions autonomously. Must ask for creative direction, never propose defaults for sound/naming/aesthetics.

phases.description: Define exactly what you're building before writing any code. AI should be ASKING YOU questions, not proposing solutions.
phases.next_phase_context: Complete specification with all creative decisions locked. Ready for architecture planning.

checklist.task: Define plugin type and signal flow
checklist.instruction: Plugin type (synth/effect/analyzer/hybrid), signal flow, DSP chain order, parameter count. AI NEVER proposes a signal flow unprompted.
Reference plugins/hardware, genre context, character words, uniqueness. Record exact words as creative north star. Never paraphrase.
Lock: JUCE version, formats (VST3/AU/AAX/Standalone), target OS (ALL), target DAW, sample rates (44.1k-192kHz), buffer size range, CPU budget.
Define when hot signals are OK vs not. Audit existing gain staging before proposing changes.
Define creative direction for presets. User approves every name individually.
Structured doc: architecture, DSP with code, GUI with dimensions/colors, parameters, presets, build instructions, 'what not to do' section.
Check: placeholder values, contradictions, ambiguity, scope gaps, formula correctness. Verify formulas at boundary conditions (param=0, param=1, param=max).

prevention_rules.lesson: AI proposed generic preset names — user rejected
prevention_rules.prevention: ALWAYS use user's exact creative language

prevention_rules.lesson: 6 layers of conservative gain staging identified as root cause of 'effect not noticeable'
prevention_rules.prevention: Always audit existing gain staging early

prevention_rules.lesson: Wavefolder formula sin(x*PI)/1.0 amplifies by PI at drive=0
prevention_rules.prevention: Always verify formulas at boundary conditions

phase_gate: Plugin type and signal flow defined
Sound identity documented in YOUR words (not paraphrased by AI)
Technical constraints locked (JUCE version, formats, ALL target OS, DAW)
Preset theme chosen with creative names you approve

phases.description: Before ANY new features, audit the existing codebase for memory/CPU/thread-safety issues. Skip for brand-new plugins.
phases.next_phase_context: Existing code clean. Ready for new architecture.

checklist.instruction: Scan for non-atomic shared state between audio/GUI threads. Use std::atomic<bool> for all cross-thread flags.
checklist.validation: No issues found or all fixed

checklist.instruction: Check for static variables shared across instances. All state must be per-instance members.
Search for heap allocations, large memsets, string construction on audio thread.
Check for O(N) parameter lookups on audio thread. Cache parameter indices at init time.

prevention_rules.lesson: First cache attempt keyed on names (still O(N) to compute key)
prevention_rules.prevention: Verify ENTIRE call chain is O(1)

prevention_rules.lesson: static int lastPreset shared across all instances — data race
prevention_rules.prevention: All state must be instance members

prevention_rules.lesson: GlitchEngine cleared 1MB buffer on audio thread
prevention_rules.prevention: Pre-allocate all buffers in prepareToPlay

prevention_rules.lesson: std::unordered_map::find() can allocate via std::string construction
prevention_rules.prevention: Use std::vector<std::pair<>> for audio-thread lookups

phase_gate: No non-atomic shared state between audio/GUI threads
No static variables shared across instances
No heap allocations in processBlock path
Parameter lookups are O(1) on audio thread

phases.description: Turn the spec into a buildable plan with complete code.
phases.next_phase_context: Complete implementation plan. Ready for build setup.

checklist.instruction: AI must read EVERY source file before planning. No planning from memory.

Class diagram: processor, editor, DSP modules, parameter layout, state management. APVTS for all parameters, processBlock thread-safe, Editor talks to Processor ONLY through APVTS, DSP modules self-contained with prepare()/reset()/process().
For each block: algorithm choice, math, JUCE implementation path, CPU cost, gotchas. VERIFY all formulas at boundary conditions.

checklist.task: Break into ordered task list with code
checklist.instruction: Each task: ONE thing, files to modify, JUCE classes used, ACTUAL CODE, build command, commit message. Ordered by dependency.
Check: scope completeness, dependency order, type consistency, formula correctness at boundaries, buffer sizes at max sample rate (192kHz).

prevention_rules.lesson: Plan specified Q constant 24.5f when correct was 49.5f
prevention_rules.prevention: Always compute formula output at param=0 and param=1

prevention_rules.lesson: Plan was 1577 lines — too large for single response
prevention_rules.prevention: Write in chunks using Write + Edit. Use unique anchor strings to avoid multi-match errors

prevention_rules.lesson: Plan self-review MISSED FHT placement, buffer overflow, and Q constant errors
prevention_rules.prevention: Self-review is necessary but NOT sufficient — two-stage review during implementation catches what self-review misses

phase_gate: Every spec requirement has a corresponding task
Each task has complete code and build step
All DSP formulas verified at boundary conditions
Buffer sizes computed for max supported sample rate (192kHz)

phases.description: Set up build system, test framework, and CI before writing DSP code.
phases.next_phase_context: Build system ready, tests pass. Ready for DSP implementation.

checklist.instruction: Version, source files, JUCE modules, target formats (VST3 + Standalone min), C++17, COPY_PLUGIN_AFTER_BUILD.
Catch2 or GoogleTest. Minimum tests: plugin instantiation, parameter range validation, processBlock smoke (silence + noise), extreme params, state round-trip, multi-instance.
GitHub Actions: Linux (required), macOS (recommended), Windows (recommended). Run tests after build.

prevention_rules.lesson: GTK headers not found in tests
prevention_rules.prevention: Remove GUI-related compile definitions from test target, use minimal module set

prevention_rules.lesson: createPluginFilter() undefined in tests

phase_gate: CMakeLists.txt configured for all target formats
Test framework integrated and basic tests pass

phases.description: Build the audio engine module by module with two-stage review after each.
phases.next_phase_context: All DSP modules implemented and tested. Ready for processor integration.
preflight_checks: EM-03: In any FDN implementation, verify mixing matrix is in FEEDBACK path, not just output
EM-04: Compute max delay length at 192kHz: max_base * (192000/48000). Buffer must be >= this
EM-06: All circular buffer indices use & mask wrapping
EM-08: Verify filter Q mapping at reso=0 and reso=1

checklist.task: Implement DSP modules with two-stage review
checklist.instruction: For EACH module: (1) implement, (2) spec compliance review, (3) code quality review, (4) if issues: fix + re-review BOTH stages.

checklist.task: Run automated tests after each module
checklist.instruction: Compilation succeeds, processBlock smoke test passes.

two_stage_review.description: This is the single most important quality gate in the playbook.
two_stage_review.evidence: Code quality reviewer caught EM-03 (FHT not in feedback — critical), EM-04 (buffer overflow), EM-05/06/07 (3 GlitchEngine bugs), EM-08 (Q constant). Spec reviewer alone would have missed ALL of these.

phase_gate: Each module passed two-stage review (spec + code quality)
All critical and important issues resolved

phases.description: Implement presets AND state save/restore. State persistence is NOT optional.
phases.next_phase_context: State persistence working. Ready for processor integration.

checklist.instruction: CRITICAL: getStateInformation and setStateInformation must be implemented, not empty stubs. Test: save project in Reaper, close, reopen — all parameters restored.
Add new fields to struct, populate from spec. Values are AI-generated but must be auditioned in Phase 9.
Add new params to capture/apply. Log-space interpolation for frequency params, cosine for mix. Choice params snap at 50%. Bools not morphed.

state_pattern.save: void getStateInformation(juce::MemoryBlock& dest) { auto state = apvts.copyState(); auto xml = state.createXml(); copyXmlToBinary(*xml, dest); }
state_pattern.restore: void setStateInformation(const void* data, int size) { auto xml = getXmlFromBinary(data, size); if (xml && xml->hasTagName(apvts.state.getType())) apvts.replaceState(juce::ValueTree::fromXml(*xml)); }

prevention_rules.lesson: Epiphany Machine v3 shipped with empty stubs
prevention_rules.prevention: Broken state save = lost presets = angry users — always implement

prevention_rules.lesson: Linear mix blend — only first 30% effective
prevention_rules.prevention: Use equal-power (cosine) dry/wet mixing

phase_gate: Preset count consistent across PresetData, APVTS, PresetManager
Morph interpolation uses log-space for frequencies, cosine for mix

phases.description: Wire DSP modules together in processBlock.
phases.next_phase_context: All parameters wired, signal flowing. Ready for GUI.
preflight_checks: EM-13: EVERY SmoothedValue must have getNextValue() called per-sample. Audit ALL declarations
EM-09: Copy formula constants from spec exactly — no rounding
EM-10: Every feedback loop must have a safety limiter (soft-clip or hard-clip)
EM-11: getTailLengthSeconds() must return max decay parameter value
EM-15: Default decay should be <=2.0s so parameter changes are audible quickly

checklist.instruction: All parameters with correct ranges, defaults, skew values. Frequency: skew 0.3. Decay/feedback: skew 0.5.
Full signal flow per spec. After writing, grep for getNextValue() in per-sample loops. Any missing = dead parameter.
List every SmoothedValue in header. For each: declared? initialized in prepareToPlay? setTargetValue per block? getNextValue per sample? Value used downstream?

smoothedvalue_audit_checklist: getNextValue() called per-sample in a loop
Ramp time: 20ms for continuous params, 42ms for bypass/mode transitions
phase_gate: SmoothedValue audit: every SmoothedValue has getNextValue() per-sample

Every parameter control uses APVTS Attachment. Timer-based updates for value labels. Verified bounds arithmetic.
Load plugin, look at it, describe changes. Timebox: 2 sessions max. Ship what you have.

prevention_rules.lesson: GUI component overflows parent panel
prevention_rules.prevention: Walk the bounds arithmetic: panelY + componentY + componentHeight <= panelY + panelHeight

gui_performance_patterns: setOpaque(true) when component fills bounds completely — prevents parent repaint cascade
setBufferedToImage(true) for expensive static visuals (leaf components only)
JUCE 7.0.6+: Use juce::VBlankAttachment instead of Timer for frame-synced UI updates
JUCE_LIVE_CONSTANT(value) for runtime tuning without recompiling
Treat paint() like audio thread — minimize allocations, pre-allocate Path/Image/ColourGradient as members
phase_gate: All parameters have GUI controls with APVTS attachments
All controls visible and within bounds
YOU have approved the visual design

phases.description: Verify the plugin builds and works across all target platforms and configurations.
phases.next_phase_context: Plugin validated. Ready for DAW testing.

checklist.instruction: Clean build, run tests, verify .vst3 binary exists.
Build via CI or cross-compilation. At minimum verify CMakeLists.txt is correct.
44.1kHz, 48kHz, 96kHz, 192kHz. No buffer overflows, no NaN, no corruption.
64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048. No crashes, no glitches.
All params at min, all at max. No crashes, no NaN, no inf.
4+ instances simultaneously. No cross-talk, no shared state corruption.
Save Reaper project, close, reopen. All parameters match.
git tag vX.Y.Z

prevention_rules.lesson: DiffusionNetwork kBufSize=4096 overflowed at 96kHz+
prevention_rules.prevention: Always test at max supported sample rate

prevention_rules.lesson: static int lastPreset shared across instances
prevention_rules.prevention: Never use static for mutable state

phase_gate: Linux build succeeds with zero errors

phases.description: Load in Reaper, LISTEN, and fix what you find. This is where real bugs surface and YOU approve the sound.
phases.critical_insight: EM-13, EM-14, EM-15 were caught by USER in DAW testing, not by any automated review. Two-stage review catches implementation bugs but CANNOT catch perceptual/UX issues. DAW testing by the human is irreplaceable.

checklist.task: Load in Reaper and play audio
checklist.instruction: Load plugin, play audio, describe what you hear. AI cannot evaluate sound.
Move EVERY knob while audio plays. Does each produce audible change? Report dead or delayed controls.
Sweep mix 0->1. Is change evenly distributed or bunched at one end?
Load EVERY preset. Does it sound good? Showcase range? Usable? Mark any needing tuning.
Record automation on 2-3 parameters, play back. No clicks, no zippers, smooth transitions.
Toggle bypass — clean? Toggle freeze — infinite sustain without explosion? Freeze + high drift + high feedback — safety limiter works?
Read processBlock, trace signal flow, identify root cause, implement fix, rebuild, user re-tests.

prevention_rules.lesson: DRIVE knob was dead because SmoothedValue never advanced — silent bug, no crash, no error
prevention_rules.prevention: Audit EVERY SmoothedValue

prevention_rules.lesson: Linear mix blend concentrated change in first 30% of range
prevention_rules.prevention: Equal-power cosine mixing

prevention_rules.lesson: Controls seemed delayed because 4.0s default decay masked changes
prevention_rules.prevention: Default decay <= 2.0s

phase_gate: Plugin loads in Reaper without crashing
EVERY control produces audible/visible change when moved
Mix knob effective across full range
ALL presets auditioned — usable ones approved, broken ones fixed or removed
No audio glitches, clicks, or dropouts

phases.description: Package, copy binary, push to repo.

checklist.instruction: cp compiled .so/.vst3 to project root for easy GitHub download. Commit it.
What the plugin does, system requirements, install instructions per OS, parameter reference, quick start. If manual exists, update it.
Push all commits + tag. Pull first if remote diverged.

prevention_rules.lesson: Git push rejected — remote diverged
prevention_rules.prevention: Always git pull before pushing a large batch. For binary merge conflicts, use git checkout --ours or --theirs explicitly

phase_gate: Binary at project root (Linux .so at minimum)

phases.description: Make it fast and stable. Profile before optimizing.

checklist.instruction: Profile processBlock with perf (Linux), Instruments (macOS), VTune (Windows). Identify top 3 hotspots. Do NOT optimize without profiling first.
No heap allocations in processBlock, no memory leaks, all buffers pre-allocated in prepareToPlay.
Process 60s of silence. CPU should remain near-zero. Use BOTH ScopedNoDenormals AND 1e-18 offset in feedback paths.
LISTEN after every optimization. Confirm sound hasn't changed. Never sacrifice sound quality for CPU.

optimization_targets: Per-sample transcendental functions (pow, sin, tan, exp) — pre-compute per block where possible
Cache-unfriendly access patterns in delay line arrays
Unnecessary computations when parameters haven't changed
phase_gate: Denormal stress test passes (60s silence, CPU stable)

phases.description: What worked, what didn't. Extract templates for next plugin.
phases.next_phase_context: Complete. Ready for next plugin or version.

checklist.instruction: Which phases took longest? Where did AI produce best code first try? Where did most iteration burn? What to add to playbook?
Custom DSP blocks, LookAndFeel, APVTS boilerplate, build config, test framework. Save as template or personal JUCE module.
Add lessons learned, new failure modes, updated prevention rules. Each build should improve the playbook.
Features cut, user feedback, new ideas, deferred improvements. Becomes Phase 0 input for next run.

failure_modes.description: Comprehensive failure mode database combining generic JUCE issues (FM-xx), session-specific bugs from Epiphany Machine (EM-xx), and session-specific bugs from CogVST development.

numbering_systems.FM_xx: Generic JUCE failure modes — common across all plugin projects
numbering_systems.EM_xx: Epiphany Machine session-specific bugs — real bugs from v3 build
numbering_systems.CM_xx: CogVST session-specific bugs — real bugs from CogVST development

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Audio dropouts, glitches, occasional crashes
generic_failure_modes.cause: Heap allocation on audio thread (new, delete, std::vector::push_back, juce::String, DBG())
generic_failure_modes.fix: Pre-allocate all buffers in prepareToPlay(). Use juce::SmoothedValue instead of creating objects per sample.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Code review checklist item. Run pluginval (tests for this). Use juce::ScopedNoDenormals as reminder anchor.
generic_failure_modes.detection: pluginval strictness 5+, Perfetto profiling shows allocation stalls

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Crash or memory corruption at 96kHz or 192kHz
generic_failure_modes.cause: Fixed-size buffers calculated for 48kHz; delay lines too short for higher rates
generic_failure_modes.fix: Scale all buffer sizes by sampleRate / 48000.0 or use maximum expected rate.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Test at 44.1k, 48k, 96k, 192k. Calculate buffer sizes in prepareToPlay() from actual sample rate.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: All parameters reset to defaults when DAW session is reopened
generic_failure_modes.cause: Forgetting to implement state save/restore (left as stubs)
generic_failure_modes.fix: Implement APVTS state serialization (see patterns reference)
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Plugin brief template requires state persistence decision. pluginval tests round-trip.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: CPU spikes to 100% when processing silence or very quiet signals
generic_failure_modes.cause: Subnormal floating-point values in feedback loops or filters
generic_failure_modes.fix: juce::ScopedNoDenormals at top of processBlock. DC offset in feedback paths.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Always include ScopedNoDenormals. Test by processing 60 seconds of silence and monitoring CPU.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Audio grows to infinity, NaN/Inf in output, loud noise
generic_failure_modes.cause: Feedback gain >= 1.0, or accumulation of gain through loop components
generic_failure_modes.fix: Clamp feedback to 0.95 max. Add soft-clip (x / (1 + |x|)) in feedback path. Apply tanh() at output.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Never allow feedback parameter to reach 1.0. Always have output limiter.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Crash when plugin editor is closed and re-opened in DAW
generic_failure_modes.cause: addListener() called without matching removeListener() in destructor
generic_failure_modes.fix: Every addListener/addChangeListener must have matching remove* in destructor
generic_failure_modes.prevention: pluginval tests editor open/close cycles. Search for addListener without matching remove.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Intermittent crashes, data races, UI freezes
generic_failure_modes.cause: Calling repaint(), heavy computation, or non-atomic operations from parameterChanged() (which can run on audio thread)
generic_failure_modes.fix: Set std::atomic<bool> flag in callback, check in Timer or VBlankAttachment
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Never do anything non-trivial in parameter callbacks

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Silent right channel when plugin receives mono input
generic_failure_modes.cause: Not copying channel 0 to channel 1 for mono inputs
generic_failure_modes.fix: Check buffer.getNumChannels() and copy: buffer.copyFrom(1, 0, buffer, 0, 0, numSamples)
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Always handle mono input in processBlock. Test with mono tracks.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Parameters don't smooth (zipper noise on automation)
generic_failure_modes.cause: Calling getCurrentValue() instead of getNextValue() per sample, or not calling it every sample
generic_failure_modes.fix: Call getNextValue() exactly once per sample in the processing loop
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Code review. Never use getCurrentValue() in processBlock.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Filters sound wrong after sample rate changes, wrong decay times at different rates
generic_failure_modes.cause: Calculating filter coefficients once and not updating in prepareToPlay()
generic_failure_modes.fix: Recalculate all sample-rate-dependent values in prepareToPlay(), which is called on rate changes
generic_failure_modes.prevention: All DSP module prepare() methods should accept sample rate and recalculate

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Audible click when toggling bypass or switching processing modes
generic_failure_modes.cause: Discontinuity in output level at the switch point
generic_failure_modes.fix: Smooth bypass transitions using SmoothedValue over ~42ms (0.042s / ~512 samples at 48kHz). Use ~20ms for continuous parameter smoothing.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Never hard-switch between dry and wet. Always crossfade.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Buffer overrun or underrun, intermittent crashes
generic_failure_modes.cause: Assuming processBlock always receives exactly samplesPerBlock samples
generic_failure_modes.fix: Always use buffer.getNumSamples() for the actual count, not the prepared block size
generic_failure_modes.prevention: samplesPerBlock in prepareToPlay() is a hint, not a guarantee

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Harsh, metallic artifacts from distortion or waveshaping
generic_failure_modes.cause: Waveshaping without oversampling creates harmonic foldback
generic_failure_modes.fix: Use dsp::Oversampling (2x or 4x) around waveshaping stages, or use ADAA techniques
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Always oversample when applying nonlinear transfer functions, especially with high-frequency content

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Volume dip at 50% wet/dry mix
generic_failure_modes.cause: Linear crossfade: dry*(1-mix) + wet*mix loses 3dB at center
generic_failure_modes.fix: Equal-power: dryGain = cos(mix * PI/2); wetGain = sin(mix * PI/2)
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Always use equal-power for dry/wet mixing

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Plugin doesn't appear in DAW's plugin list (macOS AU format)
generic_failure_modes.cause: Plugin not in correct location; AU cache not refreshed
generic_failure_modes.fix: Copy to ~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/. Run killall -9 AudioComponentRegistrar
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Set COPY_PLUGIN_AFTER_BUILD TRUE in CMake. Test in fresh DAW session.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Automation data breaks when loading old sessions after parameter changes
generic_failure_modes.cause: VST3 uses hashed parameter IDs; changing ID strings breaks backward compatibility
generic_failure_modes.fix: Never change parameter ID strings after release. Add new parameters, deprecate old ones.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Lock parameter IDs in the plugin brief before v1.0 release

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Crash on plugin close, especially on Windows
generic_failure_modes.cause: LookAndFeel destroyed before components that reference it
generic_failure_modes.fix: Declare LookAndFeel members BEFORE component members in class (destructors run in reverse order)
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Member ordering convention: LookAndFeel first, then components, then attachments

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Multiple plugin instances interfere with each other
generic_failure_modes.cause: Using static variables or singletons (DAWs may run multiple instances in one process)
generic_failure_modes.fix: Store all state as instance members, pass through component hierarchy
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Never use static for mutable state. Never use singletons in plugins.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Jerky, flickering UI, high CPU from GUI thread
generic_failure_modes.cause: Calling repaint() too frequently or on too-large regions; transparent components triggering parent repaints
generic_failure_modes.fix: Use setOpaque(true) where possible. Use setBufferedToImage(true) for expensive static visuals. Repaint only dirty regions.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Enable JUCE_ENABLE_REPAINT_DEBUGGING=1 during development. Use Perfetto for UI profiling.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Plugin fails to load on some Windows systems
generic_failure_modes.cause: Dynamically linked MSVC runtime not present on target machine
generic_failure_modes.fix: Statically link runtime: set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>)
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Always statically link on Windows. Verify with dumpbin /dependents.

generic_failure_modes.symptom: Mysterious build failures, missing headers (e.g., TargetConditionals.h on macOS)
generic_failure_modes.cause: Stale CMake cache after Xcode/compiler update
generic_failure_modes.fix: rm -rf build/ and reconfigure
generic_failure_modes.prevention: CI should always build from clean state

generic_failure_modes.symptom: User can't verify they have the latest version
generic_failure_modes.cause: Version not propagated from CMake to plugin binary
generic_failure_modes.fix: Use project(PluginName VERSION x.y.z) in CMake, reference PROJECT_VERSION in code
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Embed build timestamp/type in UI: __DATE__, __TIME__, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE

generic_failure_modes.symptom: CI pipeline fails on pluginval step
generic_failure_modes.cause: Listener leaks, assertion failures, state round-trip failures, excessive CPU in processBlock
generic_failure_modes.fix: Run pluginval locally with debugger attached. Use random seed from CI output to reproduce.
generic_failure_modes.prevention: Run pluginval locally before pushing. Include in CI pipeline from day one.

epiphany_machine_bugs.description: Cache keyed on names not IDs — still O(N)
epiphany_machine_bugs.prevention: Verify ENTIRE call chain is O(1)

juce_patterns.description: Reusable JUCE API patterns extracted from sessions and documentation.

rules: No heap allocation in processBlock (new, delete, std::vector::push_back, juce::String)
No locks on audio thread (std::mutex, juce::CriticalSection)
No blocking operations (file I/O, network, sleep)
std::unordered_map::find() can allocate via std::string key — use flat arrays
NEVER use juce::AsyncUpdater from audio thread — it is NOT lock-free. Use std::atomic<bool> + Timer instead

apvts_setup.description: AudioProcessorValueTreeState is the standard way to manage parameters

gain_db.notes: Linear in dB is already log-perception

callbacks.rule: parameterChanged() and parameterValueChanged() can execute on ANY thread including audio

pattern.loop: const float v = smoothed.getNextValue(); // per sample

ramp_times.snap: setCurrentAndTargetValue() only in prepareToPlay() or when loading state

smoothed_value.critical_note: getCurrentValue() alone does NOT advance the smoother — must call getNextValue()

state_save_restore.description: Every plugin MUST implement getStateInformation and setStateInformation

mono_input_handling.description: Handle mono input by copying channel 0 to channel 1

equal_power_mixing.description: Cosine/sine crossfade for perceptually even mixing
equal_power_mixing.note: ALWAYS use equal-power, not linear. Linear concentrates change in low end.

dsp_catalog.description: DSP algorithm catalog from both Epiphany Machine and CogVST development sessions.

epiphany_machine_modules.name: DiffusionNetwork (FDN Reverb)
epiphany_machine_modules.algorithm: 8-line FDN with Fast Hadamard Transform in feedback path, RT60 decay, per-line stereo panning with LFOs
prevention_rules: EM-03: FHT must be in feedback path
epiphany_machine_modules.reference: Julius O. Smith III — Physical Audio Signal Processing: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/

epiphany_machine_modules.name: Cytomic TPT State Variable Filter
epiphany_machine_modules.algorithm: Trapezoidal SVF (Andy Simper). g=tan(pi*fc/sr), stable at all frequencies, no modulation clicks.
epiphany_machine_modules.critical_note: DO NOT use Chamberlin SVF (f=2*sin(...)). It is unstable at high frequencies and clicks during modulation.
epiphany_machine_modules.reference: Cytomic papers: https://cytomic.com/files/dsp/ — Vadim Zavalishin: The Art of VA Filter Design

epiphany_machine_modules.name: Granular Engine
epiphany_machine_modules.algorithm: Circular-buffer grain playback with adaptive envelopes (Hann >50ms, Tukey 10-50ms, Trapezoid <10ms)
prevention_rules: EM-07: No drift on reverse grains

epiphany_machine_modules.name: Wavefolder
epiphany_machine_modules.algorithm: output = input + drive * (sin(input * foldAmt * PI) / foldAmt - input). True bypass at drive=0.
prevention_rules: EM-09: Copy constants exactly from spec
EM-10: Feedback loop needs safety limiter after wavefolder

cogvst_modules.name: FastMath
cogvst_modules.algorithm: Fast approximations for expensive transcendental functions (sin, cos, tanh, exp)
cogvst_modules.cpu_cost: Very low — avoid transcendental where possible
known_issues: Approximations may introduce audible artifacts at extreme values

cogvst_modules.name: DCBlocker
cogvst_modules.algorithm: One-pole high-pass filter at ~5-20Hz to remove DC offset
known_issues: Must be first in signal chain
Don't use too high cutoff or it affects bass

cogvst_modules.name: DelayLine
cogvst_modules.algorithm: Variable-length delay with interpolation for smooth modulation
prevention_rules: CM-06: Read at writePos - delay - i
FM-02: Scale buffer for max sample rate

cogvst_modules.name: TextureBodyDetector
cogvst_modules.algorithm: Input analysis for envelope following and spectral content detection

cogvst_modules.name: Waveshaper
known_issues: FM-13: Waveshaping without oversampling creates aliasing

cogvst_modules.name: SpectralDroneEngine
cogvst_modules.algorithm: FFT-based spectral processing for drone/pad sounds
cogvst_modules.implementation: dsp::FFT with windowing and phase manipulation
known_issues: CM-08: Latency depends on fftSize * decimationFactor
cogvst_modules.sample_rate_handling: Internal rate typically 48kHz; decimation for higher rates

cogvst_modules.name: ChorusEnsemble
cogvst_modules.algorithm: Multiple modulated delay lines with LFOs for thickening/widening
cogvst_modules.implementation: Multiple DelayLine instances with modulated delay times

cogvst_modules.name: ResonantFilter
prevention_rules: EM-08: Verify Q mapping at boundaries
FM-10: Recalculate on sample rate change

cogvst_modules.name: DriveCircuit
cogvst_modules.implementation: Waveshaper followed by tone filter (shelf or tilt EQ)

cogvst_modules.name: StereoWidener
cogvst_modules.algorithm: Mid/side processing for stereo width enhancement
cogvst_modules.implementation: M = (L+R)/2, S = (L-R)/2; L' = M + width*S; R' = M - width*S
known_issues: Mono compatibility issues at extreme width

cogvst_modules.name: ModulationEngine
cogvst_modules.algorithm: LFOs and envelope generators for parameter modulation
cogvst_modules.implementation: dsp::Oscillator for LFOs, custom ADSR for envelopes
known_issues: CM-14: Compute coefficients outside per-sample loop

warm.source: Sound on Sound: Filter Design Fundamentals
warm.notes: Lower cutoff reduces high harmonics, perceived as warmth
warm.why: Lower cutoff attenuates frequencies above the cutoff point. Our ears perceive warmth when 2-8kHz content is reduced, creating a less harsh, more pleasing tone. The cutoff frequency isn't linear - use skew=0.5 for perceptually even response.

bright.source: Sound on Sound: Filter Design Fundamentals
bright.why: Higher cutoff allows more high frequency content through. Our ears perceive brightness from 2-8kHz content. A cutoff of 0.6-1.0 keeps most high harmonics, emphasizing presence and clarity.

resonant.source: Sound on Sound: Filter Design Fundamentals
resonant.why: Resonance adds a peak at the cutoff frequency, emphasizing harmonics near that point. This creates the characteristic 'squlechy' or 'singing' filter sound. High resonance (>0.7) can push the filter into self-oscillation, producing a sine wave.

muted.why: Very low cutoff removes most high frequency content, creating a muffled or 'underwater' quality. Useful for effect or for taming bright sounds. Combined with resonance can create vocal-like formants.

aggressive.notes: Combined with high cutoff for aggressive character
aggressive.why: Moderate resonance with high cutoff creates an edgy, aggressive character. The peak at cutoff frequency emphasizes upper harmonics without full self-oscillation, giving bite without uncontrollable feedback.

subtle_warmth.why: Low drive adds gentle harmonic saturation that our ears perceive as warmth. The harmonics fill in the frequency spectrum without being obvious. This is similar to analog circuit saturation.

aggressive_grit.why: High drive creates hard clipping or heavy soft clipping, producing pronounced harmonic content. This creates the 'gritty' or 'dirty' character used in aggressive genres like metal, dubstep, or industrial.

harmonic_richness.why: Medium drive adds harmonics that enhance the fundamental without being obviously distorted. This fills out the frequency spectrum and adds presence. Works well for bass and lead sounds that need to cut through.

subtle_echo.why: Medium delay times create distinct but not distracting echoes. Low feedback gives 2-3 repeats. Low mix ensures the echo supports rather than overpowers the dry signal.

rhythmic_slap.why: Short delay times (slapback) create comb filtering that thickens the sound. Low feedback gives a single strong echo. This doubles the perceived thickness without obvious delay.

atmospheric.why: Long delay times with high feedback create evolving soundscapes. The repeats build on each other, creating ambient textures. Works well for pads, drones, and atmospheric elements.

subtle_width.why: Slow rate with moderate depth creates gentle pitch modulation that widens the stereo image without obvious movement. This is the classic 'stereo widener' effect used on vocals and guitars.

lush_movement.why: Faster rate with high depth creates obvious pitch movement. This gives the characteristic 'shimmering' chorus sound. Best for pads and atmospheric sounds where movement is desired.

subtle_movement.why: Slow LFO rates (0.1-0.3 Hz) create gradual movement over 3-10 seconds. Low depth ensures the modulation is subtle, not obvious. This adds 'life' to static sounds without being distracting.

strong_modulation.why: Faster LFO rates (0.5-2 Hz) create obvious cyclic movement. High depth means the parameter sweeps through its full range. This creates pronounced effects like filter wobbling or vibrato.

conflict_resolution.description: Detects and resolves contradictory user requirements. When users request conflicting sonic qualities, this system provides guidance on resolution.

warm_and_bright.conflict: warm requires low cutoff (0.2-0.4), bright requires high cutoff (0.6-1.0)

option_a.name: Ask user to choose
option_a.suggestion: These qualities conflict. Which is more important for your sound: warmth (reduced high frequencies) or brightness (emphasized high frequencies)?

option_b.name: Middle ground
option_b.suggestion: Use neutral cutoff with slight resonance for character without committing to either extreme.

option_c.name: Alternative approach
option_c.suggestion: Consider 'warm with presence' instead: cutoff at 0.35-0.45 with slight high shelf boost.

thin_and_fat.conflict: thin requires minimal low end/width, fat requires thickness from detune/saturation/width

option_a.name: Ask user to choose
option_a.suggestion: These qualities conflict. Do you want a tight, focused sound (thin) or a wide, rich sound (fat)?

option_b.name: Middle ground
option_b.suggestion: Use moderate width without heavy detune for a balanced sound.

option_c.name: Alternative approach
option_c.suggestion: Consider 'focused but rich': single oscillator with harmonic saturation instead of detune.

aggressive_and_smooth.conflict: aggressive requires drive/distortion/harsh transients, smooth requires gentle dynamics/filtered highs

option_a.name: Ask user to choose
option_a.suggestion: These qualities conflict. Which character do you prefer: aggressive (distortion, edge) or smooth (filtered, gentle)?

option_b.name: Middle ground
option_b.suggestion: Use subtle drive with mid-range filter for controlled aggression.

option_c.name: Alternative approach
option_c.suggestion: Consider 'controlled power': aggressive transient with smooth sustain (filter envelope).

punchy_and_ambient.conflict: punchy requires fast transients/short decay, ambient requires long decay/spatial effects

option_a.name: Ask user to choose
option_a.suggestion: These qualities conflict. Do you want a rhythmic, percussive sound (punchy) or a wash of atmosphere (ambient)?

option_b.name: Layered approach
option_b.suggestion: Layer two sounds: a punchy transient layer with a separate ambient pad. Use separate synthesis or samples.

option_c.name: Alternative approach
option_c.suggestion: Consider 'evolving with attack': long ambient pad with fast attack transient from filter envelope.

subtle_and_aggressive.conflict: subtle requires minimal processing/low values, aggressive requires high drive/distortion/high values

option_a.name: Ask user to choose
option_a.suggestion: These qualities conflict. Which is more important: subtle processing or aggressive character?

option_b.name: Middle ground
option_b.suggestion: Use light drive with high resonance filter for controlled edge.

option_c.name: Alternative approach
option_c.suggestion: Consider 'refined power': subtle main processing with occasional aggressive modulation peaks.

resolution_workflow: 1. Detect conflicting descriptors in user request
- Option A: Ask user to choose primary characteristic
- Option B: Offer middle ground with parameters
4. If not in table, analyze semantically and ask clarifying question

educational_layer.description: Explains the reasoning behind parameter choices. Educational content for understanding sound design.

filter_cutoff_perception.explanation: Human hearing perceives filter cutoff logarithmically. A cutoff of 0.5 doesn't sound 'halfway' - it sounds significantly lower due to our logarithmic frequency perception. Use skewed parameter mappings to create perceptually even response.
filter_cutoff_perception.example: For even perceptual sweep: use skew=0.5 or exponential mapping

filter_resonance_self_oscillation.explanation: At high resonance values (typically >0.7 normalized), filters can self-oscillate, producing a sine wave at the cutoff frequency. This is useful for synthetic tones but can cause issues with loudness if unexpected.
filter_resonance_self_oscillation.example: For resonant bass: set resonance 0.5-0.7 to avoid self-oscillation, or embrace it for whistling tones

equal_power_crossfade.explanation: Linear crossfades cause volume drop at the midpoint. Equal power (cosine) crossfades maintain constant perceived loudness. Use for wet/dry mixing, oscillator mixing, and any amplitude crossfade.
equal_power_crossfade.example: For mix parameter: dry_gain = cos(mix * PI/2), wet_gain = sin(mix * PI/2)

detune_and_thickness.explanation: Slight pitch differences between oscillators create beating patterns that our ears perceive as 'thickness' or 'richness'. Too much detune creates obvious detuning; too little sounds static.
detune_and_thickness.example: For warm pad: detune 5-15 cents per oscillator. Use multiple oscillators with different amounts.

chorus_width_perception.explanation: Chorus creates the illusion of width through pitch modulation and delay variation. The effect is stereo-dependent and may collapse in mono. Always check mono compatibility for chorus-heavy sounds.
chorus_width_perception.example: For mono-safe width: keep chorus depth under 0.5, or use detune instead

delay_time_perception.explanation: Short delays (<50ms) create comb filtering rather than distinct echoes. Medium delays (50-200ms) create slap-back effects. Long delays (>200ms) create obvious echoes. Timing to tempo creates rhythmic effects.
delay_time_perception.example: For subtle thickening: use 20-40ms delay. For rhythmic effect: sync to tempo subdivisions.

sound_design.note: Project-specific validation logs stored in validation-logs/<project-name>/. Global patterns in validation-logs/global-patterns.json

anti_patterns.problem: Assuming linear parameter ranges produce linear perceptual changes
anti_patterns.example: Setting mix=0.5 expecting 50/50 blend, but hearing mostly wet signal
anti_patterns.solution: Use equal-power crossfade or skew factors for perceptually linear response

anti_patterns.problem: Stacking multiple gain stages without compensation leads to clipping or inaudible effects
anti_patterns.example: Drive at 0.8, filter boost at 0.6, output at 1.0 = clipped
anti_patterns.solution: Audit gain staging at each stage. Use makeup gain or compensate in DSP

anti_patterns.problem: Too many effects stacked, each adding subtle issues
anti_patterns.example: Chorus + phaser + flanger + reverb + delay = muddy, indistinct sound
anti_patterns.solution: Choose one primary modulation effect. If using multiple, reduce their depths significantly

anti_patterns.problem: Wide stereo sounds may collapse to thin/phasey in mono
anti_patterns.example: Heavy chorus + wide detune = phase cancellation in mono
anti_patterns.solution: Always check mono fold-down for any sound intended for wider release

anti_patterns.problem: Using parameter defaults without consideration for the specific sound
anti_patterns.example: Every synth preset starts at attack=0.01, decay=0.5, sustain=0.5, release=0.5
anti_patterns.solution: Consider each sound's needs. Pad? Longer attack. Percussion? Short decay. Lead? Medium envelope.

anti_patterns.problem: High resonance adds gain at cutoff frequency, causing level spikes
anti_patterns.example: Resonance at 0.8 creates +6dB peak, clips downstream
anti_patterns.solution: Reduce output gain when increasing resonance, or use compensated filter design

anti_patterns.problem: Using wrong filter type undermines sonic intent
anti_patterns.example: Trying to make bass 'tight' with highpass instead of lowpass
anti_patterns.solution: Match filter type to intent: lowpass for warmth, highpass for air, bandpass for resonant

for_new_plugin: 1. Start with Phase 0 — AI asks questions, you define the spec
2. If upgrading existing code: run Phase 1 (performance audit). If new: skip to Phase 3.
3. Phase 2: Create architecture and task breakdown
4. Phases 3-7: Implementation. Use two-stage review for each DSP module.
5. Phase 8: Build verification and stress tests
6. Phase 9: Load in DAW and LISTEN. This catches what code review cannot.
8. Phases 11-12: Optimize, retrospect, update this playbook
for_bug_fixing: 1. Identify the bug in failure_modes table
2. Follow the prevention rule for that bug
3. Use the phase checklist to ensure complete fix
